items.title: Finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification and control data
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, regarded as a
classical variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) with its
analytic topology, its smooth points (regular local rings) and its finite
smooth algebraic frontier stratifications
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]).

(a) **Whitney conditions.** Let $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ be a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification whose strata are pure-dimensional, and let $R\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ be incident strata. In local analytic charts of an ambient smooth manifold, the pair $(S,R)$ satisfies **Whitney (a)** at $y\in R$ if for every sequence $x_n\in S$ with $x_n\to y$ whose tangent planes $T_{x_n}S$ converge to a plane $T$, one has $T_yR\subseteq T$; it satisfies **Whitney (b)** at $y$ if additionally, whenever $y_n\in R$ with $y_n\to y$ and the real secant lines through $x_n,y_n$ converge to a line $\ell$, one has $\ell\subseteq T$. A **finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification** of $X$ is a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification satisfying (a) and (b) at every point of every incident pair. Coordinate independence of the limits and the implication (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), commonly used in the literature, are not assumed as proved here; requiring both conditions makes the intended interface explicit.

(b) **Tube control data.** A system of **tube control data** on the analytic stratified space $X$ consists of an open neighbourhood $T_R$ of each stratum $R$, a continuous retraction $\pi_R:T_R\to R$ and a continuous radius $\rho_R:T_R\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\rho_R^{-1}(0)=R$, both maps are smooth on each stratum, and for every incident upper stratum $S$ the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ restricts to a submersion $S\cap T_R\to R\times(0,\infty)$. On the overlap neighbourhoods where the compositions are defined one requires $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$ and $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$; every compatibility assertion must name the common domain on which the composition is defined. Tubes may be shrunk. For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

(c) **$f$-compatible tubes and controlled lifts.** Let $f:W\to B$ be a stratified submersion onto a smooth manifold. A tube system is **$f$-compatible** if $f\pi_R=f$ on the tubes used. A **controlled lift** of a smooth base field $v$ on $B$ is a field $V$ that is smooth on each stratum and satisfies $df(V)=v\circ f$, $d\pi_R(V)=V|_R\circ\pi_R$ and $d\rho_R(V)=0$ on specified controlled tube neighbourhoods. **Locally bounded** means the ambient norm is bounded on a neighbourhood of every point; this is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of the definition. **Radial controlled lifts** instead satisfy $d\rho_R(V)=\rho_R$ with fixed $\pi_R$ together with the appropriate annular overlap controls.

(d) **Conical product neighbourhoods.** A **conical product neighbourhood along $R$** is a stratum-preserving homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of a point of $R$ to $B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c(L)$ carrying $R$ to the ball times the cone apex, with compact finitely Whitney-stratified $L$. The radial and tangential transports must be compatible with the actual coefficient data when cohomological local systems are deduced; topological existence alone does not supply canonical derived-sheaf transport.

(e) **Finite triangulation of a noncompact space.** In the compactification convention used here, a **finite triangulation** of a noncompact space $X$ consists of finite simplicial complexes $D\subseteq K$ together with a homeomorphism $|K|\setminus|D|\to X$; compatibility with prescribed subsets means they are unions of interiors of retained simplices. This does not assert that algebraic morphisms become simplicial, and real simplicial dimensions do not replace the complex dimensions of the algebraic strata.
items.strategy: Every clause is a definition with its well-definedness comments; no existence of stratifications, tubes, controlled lifts or triangulations is asserted. (i) Whitney (a),(b) are stated in the standard Euclidean coordinates of chosen local affine embeddings into $\mathbb C^N$ (the affine-model convention of [[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]); the earlier analytic-topology/smoothness Definition supplies analytic topology and intrinsic regularity, not an analytic-chart comparison theorem for the strata; limits are taken in finite-dimensional Grassmannians, and coordinate independence is explicitly not claimed, so no invariant is presupposed. (ii) Tube control data impose smoothness on strata of the ambient stratified space and require compositions only where defined; shrinking is allowed, and local properness is stated as a compactness condition on closed radius ranges. (iii) Compatibility with a stratified submersion $f$ and the three differential equations for a controlled lift are conditions on a given field, not existence claims; local boundedness is flagged as an extra hypothesis. (iv) The conical product convention separates the homeomorphism statement from coefficient transport. (v) The triangulation convention is the deleted-boundary convention of noncompact finite type. All clauses are choice-free: nothing is selected, and the cited published definitions are choice-free.
items.axiom_use: None: a definitional contract; the cited definitions are choice-free and no selection is made.

items.title: Generic complex algebraic Whitney regularity
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $S,Y\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be disjoint irreducible smooth locally
closed complex algebraic varieties with $Y\subseteq\overline S$ and
$\dim Y<\dim S$. There is a proper closed algebraic subset $E\subsetneq Y$ such
that $(S,Y)$ satisfies Whitney (a) and (b) at every point of $Y\setminus E$.
Finite prescribed incident upper strata can be treated with one common
exceptional subset by taking a finite union. The same result holds in the
affine charts of a quasi-projective algebraic ambient manifold.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Put $d=\dim S$ and let $G$ be the graph of the map $(x,y)\mapsto(T_xS,[x-y])$ from $S\times Y$ to $\operatorname{Gr}(d,n)\times\mathbb P^{n-1}$; it is algebraic by [F5], because on chart domains the tangent plane is the kernel of the Jacobian matrix of local equations, whose basis entries are regular ratios on each fixed nonzero-minor chart and the secant coordinates are regular since $x\ne y$. Let $Z$ be the reduced closure of $G$ in $\overline S\times Y\times\operatorname{Gr}(d,n)\times\mathbb P^{n-1}$. The graph $G$ is isomorphic to $S\times Y$, hence irreducible by [F6], and $\overline S$, $Y$, $\operatorname{Gr}(d,n)$ and $\mathbb P^{n-1}$ are irreducible; the ambient product is therefore irreducible by [F6], and its closed subset $Z$, the closure of the irreducible $G$, is irreducible as well. Let $B=Z\setminus G$, a proper closed subset, and let $g:Z\to Y$ be the projection; it is dominant because it is onto on $G$. [F4, F5, F6, A1, construct]

2.1 Apply [F2] to $g$ to obtain a dense open subset of $Y$ over which the fibres $Z_y$ are nonempty and pure of dimension $r=\dim Z-\dim Y$. This number is positive, because each fibre contains $G_y=\{(x,y,T_xS,[x-y]):x\in S\}\cong S$ of dimension $\dim S\ge1$. Each irreducible component $B_i$ of the proper closed subset $B$ has $\dim B_i<\dim Z$ by [F4]; if $B_i\to Y$ is dominant, [F2] gives a further dense open of $Y$ over which its fibres have pure dimension $\dim B_i-\dim Y\le r-1$, and if it is not dominant we remove its image closure. Intersecting the finitely many dense opens leaves a dense open $Y^0\subseteq Y$ on which $Z_y$ is pure $r$-dimensional while $B_y$ has dimension at most $r-1$; hence no irreducible component of $Z_y$ is contained in $B_y$, and for every component $V$ of $Z_y$ the set $V\cap G_y=V\setminus B_y$ is a nonempty dense open subset of the irreducible $V$. [F2, F4, A1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Fix $y\in Y^0$ and an incidence point $z_0=(y,y,T,[u])\in Z_y$ with $u\ne0$. Let $V$ be an irreducible component of $Z_y$ containing $z_0$ and let $\gamma$ be the holomorphic arc supplied by [F3] for the variety $V$, the nonempty Zariski open $V\setminus B_y$ and the point $z_0$. Since $\gamma$ maps into $Z_y$ and $Z_y\subseteq g^{-1}(y)$, its second coordinate is the constant $y$; write $\gamma(s)=(x(s),y,T(s),[u(s)])$ with $\gamma(0)=z_0$ and $\gamma(s)\in G$ for $s\ne0$. Then $T(s)=T_{x(s)}S$ and $[u(s)]=[x(s)-y]$ for $s\ne0$, so $x(s)\ne y$ for $s\ne0$. Choosing a projective chart containing $[u]$, the normalized representative of the arc is holomorphic, and since $x(s)-y$ is not identically zero some coordinate has finite positive vanishing order; with $m\ge1$ the minimum of these orders, $x(s)-y=s^mv(s)$ with $v$ holomorphic and $v(0)\ne0$, and $[v(0)]=[u]$. [F3, A1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Let $p_0$ be a complex covector annihilating the complex plane $T$. In a Grassmannian matrix chart around $T$ write $T(s)$ as the graph of a holomorphic matrix $A(s)$ with $A(0)=A_0$, possible for small $s$ because $T(s)\to T$; every annihilator of the graph of $A(s)$ has the form $q(s)=(-A(s)^tb,b)$ for $b\in(\mathbb C^{n-d})^*$, and $b$ can be chosen with $(-A_0^tb,b)=p_0$ because $p_0$ annihilates $T$. The resulting $q(s)$ is holomorphic and annihilates each $T(s)$. Since $x(s)\in S$ for $s\ne0$, its derivative lies in $T_{x(s)}S=T(s)$ by [F5], so $q(s)(x'(s))=0$ for $s\ne0$. Differentiating $x(s)-y=s^mv(s)$ gives $x'(s)=s^{m-1}(mv(s)+sv'(s))$, and dividing by $s^{m-1}$ and letting $s\to0$ yields $p_0(mv(0))=0$, hence $p_0(v(0))=0$. Every annihilator of $T$ therefore kills $v(0)$, so $v(0)\in T$ and the limiting complex secant line $[u]$ lies in $T$. [F5, A1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Now let $x_j\in S$ and $y_j\in Y$ be sequences converging to the same point $y\in Y^0$, with tangent planes $T_{x_j}S$ converging to a plane $T$ and real secant lines through $x_j,y_j$ converging to a real line $\ell$. After choosing their signs, the secant directions normalized to unit vectors converge to a unit vector $w$ spanning $\ell$, and the complex projective points $[x_j-y_j]=[w_j]$ converge to $[w]$, the complex line spanned by $\ell$; moreover $(x_j,y_j,T_{x_j}S,[x_j-y_j])\in G\subseteq Z$ converges to $(y,y,T,[w])\in Z_y$ because $Z$ is closed. Applying steps 3.1 and 4.1 to this incidence point shows that its limiting complex secant line lies in $T$, so $w\in T$ and $\ell=\mathbb Rw\subseteq T$. This is Whitney (b) at $y$ in the full moving-point form. [F1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

6.1 For Whitney (a) at $y$, let $x_j\in S$ converge to $y$ with tangent planes converging to $T$, and let $w\in T_yY$ be a nonzero real tangent vector (the zero vector already belongs to $T$). In a holomorphic chart of the smooth manifold $Y$ near $y$ choose points $y_j\in Y$ of the form $y+\epsilon_jw+o(\epsilon_j)$ with $\epsilon_j>0$, $\epsilon_j\to0$ and $\|x_j-y\|/\epsilon_j\to0$, for instance $\epsilon_j=\sqrt{\|x_j-y\|}$ and a straight segment in the chart. Then $\|x_j-y_j\|\ge\epsilon_j\|w\|/2$ for large $j$, and the secant directions from $y_j$ to $x_j$ converge to the real line spanned by $w$. Since the tangent planes $T_{x_j}S\to T$, Whitney (b) from step 5.1 places that real line in $T$, so $w\in T$. Every real tangent vector of $T_yY$ arises in this way, so $T_yY\subseteq T$, proving Whitney (a). [F1, step 5.1, construct]

7.1 Set $E=Y\setminus Y^0$; it is a proper closed algebraic subset by step 2.1, and steps 5.1 and 6.1 show that $(S,Y)$ satisfies (a) and (b) at every point of $Y\setminus E$. For finitely many prescribed incident upper strata $S_1,\ldots,S_m$ over the same irreducible $Y$, apply the construction to each and take the union of the finitely many proper closed exceptional sets; since $Y$ is irreducible, that finite union is still proper, by [F4]. For a quasi-projective ambient manifold, use the finitely many affine ambient charts $U_\alpha$ that meet $Y$; their intersections with the irreducible $Y$ are nonempty opens. Inside each chart apply the affine result to every pair of irreducible components $(S_i,Y_j)$ of $(S\cap U_\alpha,Y\cap U_\alpha)$ with $Y_j\subseteq\overline{S_i}$ and $\dim Y_j<\dim S_i$, and for each point of an irreducible component of $Y\cap U_\alpha$ one of these pairs accounts for every sequence in $S$ converging to it after passing to a subsequence in a component. Each chart exceptional set is closed in $Y\cap U_\alpha$ and has smaller dimension than $Y$, so its closure in $Y$ is proper by [F4]. The union of these finitely many closures and the proper closed complements $Y\setminus U_\alpha$ is still proper because $Y$ is irreducible. Outside this union every chart argument applies, giving the required closed $E\subsetneq Y$. [F4, step 2.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

items.title: Complex algebraic varieties and maps admit compatible finite stratifications
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced quasi-projective complex
algebraic varieties, and prescribe finitely many closed or locally closed
algebraic subsets in source and target. There exist finite smooth complex
algebraic Whitney (a),(b) stratifications with frontier on $X$ and $Y$
respecting all prescribed subsets, such that each source stratum maps
surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. A further finite algebraic
stratification may be prescribed and refined. The analytic strata are smooth
complex manifolds and the restrictions are smooth submersions. If $f$ is proper
in the analytic topology, in particular if it is a projective algebraic
morphism, the whole restriction $f^{-1}(T)\to T$ over any target stratum is
proper; no restriction of $f$ to a nonclosed individual source stratum is
asserted proper.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Replace every prescribed locally closed subset $A$ by the two prescribed closed subsets $\overline A$ and $\overline A\setminus A$; their difference recovers $A$, and it suffices to respect the resulting finite list of closed subsets. Refine the smooth-partition construction of [F2] to construct, for a closed residual variety $R$ together with a finite list of prescribed closed subsets and finitely many previously fixed smooth strata outside $R$ whose closures must be respected, a Whitney partition of $R$ compatible with all of them: take the irreducible components $R_i$ of $R$, remove their nonsmooth loci and their intersections with the other components, and remove every prescribed closed subset not containing $R_i$, obtaining dense smooth opens $L_i$; then for every previously fixed upper stratum $S$, remove $R_i\cap\overline S$ when $R_i\not\subseteq\overline S$, and when $R_i\subseteq\overline S$ use [F3] to remove the closure in $R_i$ of the exceptional subset of [F3], which is proper because it has dimension smaller than $\dim R_i$. Finitely many upper strata leave nonempty dense smooth opens $U_i\subseteq R_i$, and [F3] makes each $U_i$ Whitney-regular with every incident previously fixed upper stratum. [F1, F2, F3, A1, construct]

2.1 Emit the $U_i$ as strata, add their closures $R_i$ to the list of closed subsets to be respected, and recurse on the closed complement $R\setminus\bigcup_iU_i$, whose dimension drops because every component lost a dense open subset. The recursion terminates by induction on dimension, producing a finite partition of $R$ into smooth irreducible locally closed strata. Strata of the same round have no frontier relation, since each $U_i$ misses all other components $R_j$. Every pair of incident strata has its upper stratum emitted earlier, and when the lower stratum was emitted step 1.1 imposed Whitney (a) and (b) with that upper stratum; boundaries have strictly smaller dimension by [F2]. The respected closures make every stratum closure a union of strata. In a quasi-projective ambient space, cover it by finitely many affine coordinate charts and apply the affine-chart version of [F3]; a sequence in $R$ converging to a point meets only finitely many components of the chart intersections, so passing to a subsequence in one component reduces the conditions to the chart version. Thus Whitney partitions compatible with a finite list of closed sets and with fixed external upper strata exist. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Construct the map-compatible partitions by decreasing target residual dimension. Start with target residual $R=Y$ and source residual $f^{-1}(R)=X$, and at each later round maintain the original closed-set lists together with the closures of all previously emitted source and target strata. Partition the source residual $f^{-1}(R)$ by step 2.1, so that it is Whitney-compatible with all previously emitted source strata. For each irreducible component $R_i$ of $R$, choose a dense smooth open $L_i\subseteq R_i$ as in step 1.1, respecting the target prescriptions and Whitney-regular with all previously emitted target strata. For every new source stratum $Z_\alpha$ compute the closure of its image in $R$; if that closure is not $R_i$, remove its intersection with $R_i$, a proper closed subset; if the closure is $R_i$, then $Z_\alpha\to R_i$ is dominant and [F4] supplies a dense open subset of $R_i$ on which the restriction is smooth and onto. Intersecting the finitely many resulting dense opens with $L_i$ gives a nonempty dense open $V_i\subseteq R_i$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Emit the $V_i$ as target strata and the nonempty pieces $Z_\alpha\cap f^{-1}(V_i)$ as source strata. Each such piece is open in the smooth irreducible stratum $Z_\alpha$, hence smooth irreducible and locally closed, and it is Whitney-regular with every incident previously fixed upper source stratum, because Whitney conditions are local and were imposed on all of $Z_\alpha$ in step 2.1; with the pieces of the same round it has no frontier relation except through closures, which the later rounds make unions of strata because every closure is added to the respected list. Each piece maps smoothly and onto $V_i$ by its selection in step 3.1, and target strata are Whitney-regular with earlier target strata since $V_i\subseteq L_i$. Source frontier relations inside $f^{-1}(\bigcup_iV_i)$ are inherited from the source partition, and a stratum closure over $R_i$ misses every $V_j$ with $j\ne i$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Remove $\bigcup_iV_i$ from $R$, restrict both residuals and both lists, add all newly emitted stratum closures to the respective lists, and repeat. The target dimension strictly decreases each round, so after finitely many rounds every target point and every source point has been placed: a source point lies over one emitted target stratum and is contained in one emitted piece. Future source partitions are chosen Whitney-compatible with every earlier source stratum by step 2.1, and future target opens are chosen Whitney-compatible with earlier target strata in step 3.1, so every incident pair is covered; the closure-bookkeeping makes all stratum closures unions of strata. Each emitted piece is irreducible and nonempty, so [F7] makes it analytically connected and identifies its analytic closure with the algebraic closure tracked by the construction. This yields finite smooth Whitney frontier stratifications of $X$ and $Y$, respecting all prescribed subsets (including the strata of any prescribed finite algebraic stratification, which were treated as prescribed sets in step 1.1), with each source stratum mapping smoothly and surjectively onto one target stratum. [F1, F2, F3, F7, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 The analytic clauses follow from [F5] and the same locally standard smooth Jacobian charts: the strata are smooth complex manifolds, and each smooth restriction is, in those charts, a holomorphic map whose differential is onto and whose rank is locally constant, hence a submersion. If $f$ is proper in the analytic topology and $T$ is a target stratum, then for every compact subset $C\subseteq T$ the inclusion $T\hookrightarrow Y$ is continuous, so $C$ is compact in $Y$, and $f^{-1}(C)\subseteq f^{-1}(T)$ is compact by properness of $f$; hence the restriction $f^{-1}(T)\to T$ is proper, although individual source strata inside $f^{-1}(T)$ may fail to be closed. Empty spaces and empty prescribed families add no strata, and no tube control, isotopy or triangulation existence is claimed. [F5, A1, step 5.1, given]

7.1 For the projective case factor $f$ as a closed algebraic embedding $i:X\hookrightarrow Y\times\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$ followed by the projection $\pi:Y\times\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)\to Y$. Complex projective space is the continuous image of the unit sphere in $\mathbb C^{N+1}$ under $z\mapsto[z]$, hence compact by [F6]. A closed algebraic embedding is analytically closed, because in each chart its defining polynomial equations have continuous coefficients and their common zero set is closed. For a compact $C\subseteq Y$ the set $\pi^{-1}(C)=C\times\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C)$ is compact by [F6], and $f^{-1}(C)=i^{-1}(C\times\mathbb P^N(\mathbb C))$ is a closed subset of it, hence compact. Therefore $f$ is analytically proper, and step 6.1 applies; this is the analytic properness used by the consumers. [F6, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Whitney normal tubes have submersive radius and bounded stratumwise lifts
items.statement: Assume AC. Let a finite smooth Whitney (a),(b) stratification be embedded in $\mathbb R^N$, let $R$ be one stratum, and choose its ordinary Euclidean normal tube with projection $\pi$ and distance $r(x)=\|x-\pi(x)\|$. Near every point of $R$, after shrinking the tube, the pair $(\pi,r)$ is a submersion on each incident upper stratum. There are smooth stratumwise right inverses for its differential whose norms are locally uniformly bounded near $R$. Consequently a smooth bounded field $w$ on $R$ has smooth locally bounded lifts on each incident stratum with $d\pi(V)=w\circ\pi$ and $dr(V)=0$; there are also radial lifts with $d\pi(V_{\mathrm{rad}})=0$, $dr(V_{\mathrm{rad}})=r$ and $\|V_{\mathrm{rad}}\|\le Cr$. These are lifts relative to this one lower stratum only; no simultaneous Mather control identities or continuous stratified flow is claimed.
items.strategy: In the Euclidean tube write $x=y+n$ with $y=\pi(x)$, $n\perp T_yR$ and $r=\|n\|$, so that $dr(v)=\langle n/r,v\rangle$. For a point $x$ in an incident stratum $S$ consider the matrix $A_x$ of $(d\pi_x,dr_x)$ in a smooth lower-frame; if the lower singular value of $A_x$ failed to be locally bounded below, a contrary sequence would converge to a limiting upper plane $T$ and unit normal direction $u$ with $u\perp T_yR$; Whitney (a) puts $T_yR\subseteq T$ and Whitney (b) puts the radial limit $u$ in $T$ ([[def-finite-complex-algebraic-whitney-stratification-and-control-data]]), so $\|A^*(a,b)\|=\|P_T(a+bu)\|=1$ cannot tend to zero. This uniform bound makes $(\pi,r)$ submersive on every incident upper stratum and makes the explicit right inverse $H_x=A_x^*(A_xA_x^*)^{-1}$ smooth with locally bounded norm, giving the claimed horizontal and radial lifts; the tube and its normal coordinates are supplied by [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]], whose countable-choice hypothesis is met by the declared AC through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. Lifts of different strata are not glued, so no simultaneous compatibility is asserted.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through the chain AC => DC => AC_omega ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]), which supplies the countable-choice hypothesis of the Euclidean tubular neighbourhood theorem [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]. The singular-value argument and the lifts are otherwise explicit.

items.title: Relative tubular neighborhoods preserve a chain of submersions
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $S\subseteq\mathbb R^N$ be an embedded smooth manifold and let
$F_i:U_i\to B_i$ be a finite family of smooth submersions such that
$F_i|_{S\cap U_i}$ is a submersion. Prescribe closed subsets
$C_i\subseteq S\cap U_i$, closed relative to $S$. Suppose the maps relevant at
each $s\in S$ form a chain: on a neighborhood of $s$, every $F_i$ with
$s\in C_i$ factors smoothly through a single maximal such map $F_j$. Then a
tubular retraction $\pi:T\to S$ can be chosen so that
$$F_i(x)=F_i(\pi(x))$$
whenever $\pi(x)\in C_i$ and $x$ lies sufficiently close to its zero-section
point in the chosen tube. Its tube map is a smooth embedding from a
variable-radius neighborhood of the normal quotient bundle. Additional
prescribed positive size bounds that have a positive lower bound near every
base point can be imposed on its displacement and fiber radius; in particular,
positive continuous bounds are admissible. No convex average of manifold-valued retractions is used.
items.strategy: At each $s$ choose adapted coordinates $(b,u,z)$ with $S=\{z=0\}$ and the maximal active map $F_j=b$, straightening $S$ and applying the constant-rank normal form to the restricted submersion ([[thm-constant-rank-theorem-for-manifolds]]); the vertical quotient $Q=T\mathbb R^N|_S/TS$ receives a smooth splitting whose image is vertical for every active $F_i$. Patch the local vertical fields with a locally finite smooth partition subordinate to the local chain neighbourhoods ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]) to obtain a field $W(s,v;x)$ linear in $v$ with $W(s,v;s)=j_s(v)$ whose quotient is $v$ and which is vertical for every active constraint near $x=s$; the countable-choice hypotheses of the partition and of the Euclidean tube theorem are met by the declared AC through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]. The time-one endpoint $E(s,v)$ is smooth with $E(s,0)=s$ and $d_vE(s,0)=j_s$, hence a local diffeomorphism by [[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]; on the zero section its differential is the tubular splitting. A Lipschitz injectivity-radius argument and a smooth minorant of the resulting positive local bounds (again [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]) make $E$ an injective local diffeomorphism onto a tube, and the constraints give $F_i(E(s,v))=F_i(s)$ wherever the active chain applies. All radius requirements are positive local requirements on $S$, and prescribed size bounds can be enforced by shrinking the minorant.
items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through AC => DC => AC_omega ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) for the countable-choice hypotheses of the partition-of-unity theorem [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]] and the Euclidean tubular neighbourhood theorem [[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The ODE and constant-rank arguments are choice-free.

items.title: Whitney stratifications admit compatible control data
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $W\subseteq\mathbb R^N$ have a finite smooth Whitney (a),(b) frontier stratification by locally closed embedded strata. There are tube control data $(T_S,\pi_S,\rho_S)$, with $\rho_S$ a squared bundle radius, such that incident overlap compositions are defined and satisfy $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$, $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$. Incomparable strata have disjoint tubes, $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ is a submersion on incident upper strata, and the tube data have local properness over compact lower-stratum slices. If a smooth ambient map $f$ is a submersion on every stratum, the tubes can additionally satisfy $f\pi_S=f$. The statement is about compatible data; continuous controlled flows are a separate construction.
items.strategy: Induct on stratum dimension, retaining outer tubes while shrinking final domains, and impose displacement bounds by $\frac13$ of the distance to the frontier and to incomparable closures ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]] gives smooth positive minorants of the resulting local bounds). The displacement bound forces convergent tube points based near the frontier to share their frontier limit, and the incomparable bound makes incomparable tubes disjoint, so active lower controllers always form a chain. Near a new stratum $S$ use inner/middle/outer variable radius bands: the closure of the middle band intersected with $S$ is relatively closed, the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ is submersive on $S$ by [[lem-whitney-normal-tubes-have-submersive-radius-and-bounded-stratumwise-lifts]], and lower controllers factor through the maximal active one, so [[lem-relative-tubular-neighborhoods-preserve-a-chain-of-submersions]] applies to produce a tube preserving all active $F_R=(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ (and a given stratified submersion $f$, adjoined as a root controller). Explicit support functions supported on the middle bands and positive on the inner closures, together with the displacement bound, ensure every point of the new tube in an inner band has its base in the compatibility domain; then restrict old tubes to their inner bands and rescale. Comparing the constructed tube with an ordinary Euclidean tube by a smooth ambient diffeomorphism ([[thm-euclidean-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem]]) and applying the previous submersion statement makes $(\pi_S,\rho_S)$ submersive on incident upper strata; Whitney (a),(b) are preserved by smooth ambient diffeomorphisms. Local properness is explicit in the bundle model over compact base slices. AC meets the countable-choice hypotheses of the partition and tube suppliers through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

items.title: Controlled stratified submersions have continuous local trivializations
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $W$ be a locally closed finite Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth ambient manifold, and let $f:W\to B$ be the restriction of a smooth ambient map that is a submersion on every stratum. Every smooth base field admits, after tube shrinking, a stratumwise smooth locally bounded controlled lift. Its stratumwise ODE solutions form a jointly continuous stratum-preserving local flow with jointly continuous inverse. Each source point has a stratum-preserving product neighbourhood over a small coordinate box in $B$. If $f$ is proper, every base point has a whole-fibre stratum-preserving bundle trivialization. No global simplicial model of $f$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Construct lifts in increasing stratum dimension over the compatible tubes of [[lem-whitney-stratifications-admit-compatible-control-data]]: on a stratum use the minimum-norm right inverse of $(d\pi_R,dr_R)|_{TS}$ supplied by [[lem-whitney-normal-tubes-have-submersive-radius-and-bounded-stratumwise-lifts]] (or of $df$ where no lower controller is active), which lifts the given smooth field because $f\pi_R=f$ and respects the lower controls by the chain factorization. The minimum-norm solutions are locally bounded by a limiting surjectivity argument; patch the finitely many active controllers with a subordinate partition and inner bands, so that only linear equations in the field are summed ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]; its countable-choice hypothesis is met via [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Stratumwise ODE solutions exist and depend smoothly on parameters ([[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]); boundedness plus the compact tube slice and the radius-monotonicity argument exclude finite-time escape to lower strata, giving a common short flow interval for nearby points of possibly different strata, and the compact-slice estimates give joint continuity and a jointly continuous inverse. Ordered coordinate flows then produce stratum-preserving product neighbourhoods, and when $f$ is proper the compact inverse images bound the fields so the construction globalizes to a whole-fibre bundle trivialization.

items.title: Algebraic Whitney strata have controlled local conical neighborhoods
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety with
a finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney stratification. Its analytic
stratified space admits compatible tube control data. At every point $y$ of a
stratum $R$ there is a stratum-preserving neighborhood homeomorphism
$$U_y\cong B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c_{<1}(L_y),$$
where $L_y$ is a compact finitely Whitney-stratified real semialgebraic normal
link. The ball times cone apex is $R\cap U_y$, and upper strata correspond to
their link strata times positive radius and the ball. The local construction
can preserve a chosen ordinary normal projection and radius at $R$. Links are
locally constant in stratified homeomorphism type along $R$. Proper stratified
algebraic submersions, with their actual analytic properness, have whole-fiber
local stratified bundle trivializations; local submersions have
source-neighborhood products. No compatible triangulation or finite
sheaf-cochain model is assumed or asserted here.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Work in an affine ambient chart about $y$ and shrink it so that $X$ is closed there. Only finitely many strata have closures not containing $y$; discard a small neighbourhood meeting none of those closures, so that only $R$ and its incident upper strata remain and $R$ is the lowest local stratum. Choose the ordinary normal tube of $R$ with projection $\pi$ and distance $r$, and a relatively compact coordinate ball $B\subseteq R$ about $y$. By [F4], after shrinking over a slightly larger compact base ball, $(\pi,r)$ is submersive on all remaining upper strata for $0<r<\epsilon$. Start the local induction of [F2] with this chosen $R$-tube, so that higher tubes preserve its projection and squared radius; all finite subsequent shrinks leave a positive uniform radius over the chosen compact base ball. [F1, F2, F4, A1, construct]

2.1 Put $W^\circ=X\cap\pi^{-1}(B)\cap\{0<r<\epsilon\}$ and $g=(\pi,r):W^\circ\to B\times(0,\epsilon)$. This map is a proper stratified submersion: a compact target subset lies over a compact base subset and a closed radial interval bounded away from zero and $\epsilon$, and its inverse image is a closed subset of a compact normal disk-bundle slice inside the chart where $X$ is closed. The upper tubes are $g$-compatible by the control equations of step 1.1. Fix $0<r_0<\epsilon/3$; the reference fibre $L_y=g^{-1}(y,r_0)$ is compact, being the intersection of $X$ with the affine normal space $y+N_yR$ and the radius-$r_0$ sphere. It is real semialgebraic: in this affine chart $X$ and its algebraic strata are described by finitely many real polynomial equalities and inequalities, and the normal plane and sphere have linear and quadratic equations. [F2, F4, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 By [F3] lift coordinate fields on $B$ preserving the radial coordinate; their flows trivialize the whole reference-radius link family over a smaller base box, identifying $g^{-1}(B\times\{r_0\})$ with $B\times L_y$. Separately lift the radial base field $r\partial_r$, cut off only near the upper radial endpoint so that it equals $r\partial_r$ for $r\le r_0$; properness of $g$ supplies all lifted finite-time transports between any two positive radii in $(0,r_0]$, with time $\log(r/r_0)$ and inverse of opposite time. These flows keep $\pi$ fixed, so combining horizontal reference-radius transport with radial transport gives a stratum-preserving homeomorphism $B\times L_y\times(0,r_0)\to X\cap\pi^{-1}(B)\cap\{0<r<r_0\}$ with continuous inverse. Commutation between different chosen lifts is unnecessary because the flows are applied and reversed in a fixed order. [F3, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Extend the map of step 3.1 over cone apex points by sending $(b,\mathrm{apex})$ to $b\in R$. The distance from a transported point to its base point is exactly its ordinary normal radius $r$, so convergence to the apex is uniform over the compact link and compact base subboxes independently of the speed of the radial field; conversely, $x_j\to b\in R$ gives $\pi(x_j)\to b$ and $r(x_j)\to0$, and compactness of $L_y$ means the radial parameters converge to the apex in its quotient cone topology regardless of the link direction. Hence both the extended map and its inverse are continuous, and the image $U_y=X\cap\pi^{-1}(B)\cap\{r<r_0\}$ is open in $X$. Rescaling $r$ identifies its radial interval with $[0,1)$, yielding the displayed ball times cone; if there are no upper strata the link is empty and its cone is the single apex. [step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 The link strata are the intersections of the upper strata with the normal plane and sphere, and they are smooth by submersivity of $g$. They satisfy the frontier and Whitney conditions. For the frontier assertion, [F3] gives a source-local product for $g$ at each lower fibre point, so taking a stratum closure commutes locally with taking that fixed fibre, and the original frontier relations restrict with the same dimension drop in each stratum. For the Whitney assertion, if limiting upper tangent planes are $T$ and $K=\ker dg$ is the common fibre kernel, Whitney (a) includes the lower tangent plane in $T$, on which $dg$ is still onto, so the fibre tangent planes converge to $T\cap K$ with the expected dimension; fibre secants lie in $K$ in the limit by the first-order Taylor formula for constant $g$-values, and they lie in $T$ by Whitney (b), so they lie in $T\cap K$. This proves both conditions on the fibre, and the horizontal transport of step 3.1 identifies these finite link strata over every nearby base point, establishing local constancy of stratified homeomorphism type along $R$. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 The tube-data assertion follows from [F2] in ambient charts; for quasi-projective spaces one may use a smooth Euclidean ambient embedding of projective space by the rank-one Hermitian projector $[z]\mapsto zz^*/\|z\|^2$, whose chart inverses are coordinate ratios, and apply the same smooth construction. For an algebraic morphism over a target stratum coordinate box the smooth ambient-extension hypothesis of [F3] is supplied explicitly: regular coordinate functions of the algebraic map extend in source affine embedding charts as polynomial or localized polynomial functions, and target-stratum smooth coordinate functions extend to a target ambient neighbourhood using an ordinary tube retraction; their composites give local smooth coordinate extensions of the restricted map. Patch these Euclidean coordinate functions with [F5] on a source ambient neighbourhood; on the stratified space they all equal the original map, so their convex sum equals it and has the same tangential derivatives, and shrinking the ambient neighbourhood keeps its values in the chosen base box. Thus it is a smooth ambient extension submersive on every source stratum, and the proper whole-fibre and local source-product assertions follow from [F3] applied to these actual extensions. The complex stratum $R$ has real dimension $2\dim_{\mathbb C}R$, so the product factor has the claimed dimension, and real link or simplex dimensions do not replace it. All constructions are local or use the stated actual analytic properness. [F2, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 4.1, step 4.2] ∎

items.title: Compact controlled Whitney spaces admit commuting radial collars
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $W$ be a compact finite smooth Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth Euclidean ambient space, with the frontier condition. After shrinking compatible tube data and smoothly rescaling their squared radii by positive functions of their base projections, there are normalized tubes $T_X=\{\rho_X<1\}$ and stratum-preserving radial projections $R_X(s):T_X\setminus X\to\{\rho_X=s\}$ for $0<s<1$. On every incident overlap $Y<X$ they satisfy
$$R_X(s)R_Y(t)=R_Y(t)R_X(s),\qquad \rho_YR_X(s)=\rho_Y,\qquad \rho_XR_Y(t)=\rho_X,$$
whenever the source and target points lie in the indicated retained tubes. They also satisfy $\pi_XR_X(s)=\pi_X$, $R_X(s)R_X(t)=R_X(s)$, and $\pi_ZR_X(s)=R_X(s)|_Z\pi_Z$ for $X<Z$ on overlaps. They are continuous on their stratified domains and smooth on individual strata. For a fixed reference $a\in(0,1)$, $(R_X(a),\rho_X)$ identifies the punctured tube with $S_X(a)\times(0,1)$, where $S_X(a)=W\cap\{\rho_X=a\}$; adjoining $X$ identifies it with the corresponding open mapping cylinder of $\pi_X:S_X(a)\to X$. This is a controlled topological collar; no semialgebraicity of the resulting flows is asserted.
items.strategy: Rescale each squared radius by a positive smooth function of the base point to normalize the tube domains, which preserves the control equations and local properness over compact slices ([[lem-whitney-stratifications-admit-compatible-control-data]]). For each stratum $X$ construct a field lifting the radial target field $(0,r)$ on $W\cap T_X\setminus X$ by increasing dimension: use right inverses of $(d\pi_X,d\rho_X)$ on minimal strata and lift lower fields through intermediate controllers elsewhere; the active middle-band controllers form chains, so patching with a subordinate smooth partition preserves the linear control equations ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]; AC meets its countable-choice hypothesis via [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] and [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Integrability on all positive levels follows from a compact-trapping argument: near a lower stratum, a compact base slice with a closed radius band is invariant while the projected lower flow exists, and a finite maximal endpoint would have to approach a lower stratum with constant positive radius, which is impossible ([[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]). This produces the radial family satisfying the semigroup, projection and control equations. Commutation on incident overlaps is obtained by a decreasing-dimensional correction: conjugate the $X$ family by the already fixed $Y$ transports near the inner $Y$ band using a smooth radial reparametrisation, which is the identity near the outer boundary; the conjugation preserves all normalization, projection and control equations and commutes with $Y$ transports on the inner band. In the normalized coordinates the family identifies the punctured tube with $S_X(a)\times(0,1)$, and continuity at the adjoined zero end follows from the uniform normal-bundle estimates on compact slices.

items.title: Finite simplicial maps have explicit compatible triangulated mapping cylinders
items.statement:
Let $f:K\to L$ be a simplicial map of finite complexes; vertex identifications are allowed. Its topological mapping cylinder
$$M_f=(|K|\times[0,1]\sqcup|L|)/((x,0)\sim f(x))$$
has a finite triangulation of dimension at most $\max(\dim K+1,\dim L)$ and a homeomorphism $H$ to $M_f$ fixing both boundary copies. The triangulated cylinder retraction to $|L|$ is piecewise linear. Before triangulating, its cells and $H$ have explicit formulas. For every finite collection of pairs of subcomplexes $(K_j,L_j)$ with $f(K_j)\subseteq L_j$, the corresponding cylinders are subpolyhedra; one simultaneous subdivision makes them subcomplexes. The construction also retains the top subpolyhedron $f^{-1}(|L_j|)$ for each $L_j$. On each cell away from the collapsed end, $H$ is smooth in affine coordinates; no immersion or smooth tangent-star claim is made at a collapsed end. All boundaries may be subdivided: the lemma does not promise an extension of an arbitrarily fixed boundary triangulation without subdivision.
items.strategy: Write $z_i=\sum_{f(v)=i}x_v$ and cut each source simplex by the hyperplanes $f_i=f_j$; the resulting finite polytopal cells carry the join cells $A*C$ for the maximal vertex sets $I(C)$, with the intersection identity $(A*C)\cap(A'*C')=(A\cap A')*(C\cap C')$. Triangulate the finite polytopal complex by coning each cell from an interior point over its already triangulated boundary; the dimension bound follows from the independence of the equal-maximum equations on each image simplex. The normalized fibre coordinates $P_i(x)_v=x_v/f_i(x)$ give the explicit homeomorphism $H$, bijectivity follows from the threshold equation $\sum_i\min(z_i,m)=t$ and its inverse formulas, and continuity at the collapsed end uses compactness of $|K|$ and closedness of the quotient map; the retraction is affine on join cells, hence PL. Subcomplex pairs and the top subpolyhedra are unions of cells, and one barycentric subdivision makes them full. All facts about realizations are from [[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]], [[lem-finite-simplicial-weak-topology-agrees-with-euclidean-topology]] and [[prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization]].

items.title: Compact controlled Whitney spaces admit compatible finite triangulations
items.statement:
Assume AC. A compact finite controlled Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth
ambient space admits a finite triangulation of dimension at most the largest
real stratum dimension, compatible with every stratum closure and any
prescribed union of strata. Each open stratum is a union of open simplices. The
homeomorphism is smooth on the pieces within each stratum. The construction may
make the finitely many normal link-bundle projections between triangulated
compact stratum cores piecewise linear. It does not make an arbitrary algebraic
map globally simplicial. In particular it applies individually to
compactifications of quasi-projective complex varieties and to their compact
controlled links, once the stated Whitney/control hypotheses have been
supplied.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Let $W$ be compact with finite compatible tube data and the actual commuting radial collars of [F1]. Retain outer maps while using inner normalized domains. Fix a stratum $X$ and a level $0<a<1$; write $A=\{p\in T_X:\rho_X(p)=a\}$ and $L=\overline A$ in $W$, which is compact. A limit of points of $A$ leaving $T_X$ must land on the frontier of $X$: in tube parameters either the bases have an interior limit, which retains the tube because the normalized radius is the fixed $a<1$, or the bases approach the frontier, where the imposed displacement bound forces the point and its base to have the same limit. Consequently $L$ meets only upper incident strata, where it is the smooth hypersurface $\rho_X=a$, and lower frontier strata of $X$; it misses $X$ itself and incomparable strata. [F1, F5, A1]

2.1 Membership in $L$ on a lower frontier stratum $Y<X$ is locally constant along $Y$, by transport rather than by an appeal to a Whitney property of $L$. On a small $Y$-base coordinate box construct smooth lifts of each base coordinate field in increasing dimension, with the maximal incident tube controller as in [F1]; the field on $Y$ is the given coordinate field and upper fields satisfy $d\pi_ZV=V_Z\pi_Z$ and $d\rho_ZV=0$ on the retained tube of every lower $Z$. On the $X$-tube the lift therefore preserves $\rho_X=a$. The compact-trapping proof of [F1] gives a jointly continuous short flow even without ambient boundedness on an entire outer tube, and it maps $A$ to itself wherever defined, hence maps its closure $L$ to itself, as does the inverse flow. Ordered coordinate transports along $Y$ prove local constancy of membership, so $L\cap Y$ is an open and closed union of components of $Y$. [F1, F5, A1, step 1.1]

3.1 The same horizontal-lift construction, with the level constraints imposed in the chain of controllers, shows that the closure-incidence label of an upper level piece is locally constant on each lower level piece. If a disconnected level piece has different incidence labels, split it by the finitely many Boolean labels recording membership in the closures of the finitely many upper pieces; these subsets are open and closed smooth pieces, and since there are at most finitely many labels this makes a finite frontier stratification without assuming finitely many connected components. The maps and collars below restrict to these pieces, because the transports preserve each closure and hence its incidence labels. [F1, F5, A1, step 2.1]

4.1 For a lower frontier $Y<X$ the restricted $Y$-tube retracts $L$ into $L\cap Y$: radial $Y$-transport preserves $\rho_X$ on $A$ by the commuting collar identities, and its limit as $\rho_Y\to0$ is $\pi_Y$, so $\pi_Y(A\cap T_Y)\subseteq L$ and continuity gives the same inclusion for $L\cap T_Y$. For an upper $Y>X$ the identity $\rho_X\pi_Y=\rho_X$ shows directly that $\pi_Y$ preserves the level hypersurface. Therefore all inherited projections have their actual target in the corresponding stratum of $L$. [F1, F5, A1, step 3.1]

5.1 The inherited radius/projection maps are submersive on the smooth strata of $L$. If $Y<X<Z$, then on $Z$ the map $(\pi_X,\rho_X)$ is submersive and $(\pi_Y,\rho_Y)$ factors through $\pi_X$, while the latter pair is submersive on $X$; hence the joint map $(\pi_Y,\rho_Y,\rho_X)$ is submersive on $Z$, and restricting to $\rho_X=a$ gives the full rank of $(\pi_Y,\rho_Y)$ there. If $X<Y<Z$, then $(\pi_Y,\rho_Y)$ is submersive on $Z$ and $\rho_X$ factors through $\pi_Y$; its restriction to the kernel of $d\rho_X$ surjects onto the tangent space of $(Y\cap\{\rho_X=a\})\times(0,1)$, because lifting a target vector with $d\rho_X=0$ through the original pair and using the factorization forces the lift to satisfy the same equation. This is precisely the needed level-pair submersion. [F1, F5, A1, step 4.1]

6.1 All control equations and incomparable-domain disjointness restrict, and local properness restricts because $L$ is closed in compact $W$. The radial families restrict too: they preserve $A$ where defined, preserve its closure by continuity, and preserve the new incidence labels; their semigroup, commutation and projection equations are the original equations on actual retained domains, and zero-end convergence still follows from the compact tube estimate. Thus $L$ is a compact finite smooth controlled stratified space with commuting collars. Its maximal stratum dimension is at most $\dim(W)-1$, since upper level strata lose one dimension and lower frontier strata have dimension strictly less than $\dim X\le\dim W$; this is the dimension drop needed by the interior triangulation induction. Nothing here identifies $L$ with an algebraic or semialgebraic set. [F1, F5, A1, step 5.1]

7.1 For each stratum $Z$ define its core by removing the small open tubes of lower-dimensional strata; compactness is literal. A sequence in this core tending to the frontier of $Z$ would eventually lie in the open tube of its limiting lower stratum, contradicting the definition, so the core is a closed subset of $W$ contained in $Z$, hence compact; the same argument applies to a level link after lower-stratum tubes are removed. [F1, F5, A1, step 6.1]

8.1 At a core point the active lower controllers form a chain and the differentials of their radius functions are independent on the stratum. For a chain $Y_1<\cdots<Y_k<Z$, the submersion $(\pi_{Y_k},\rho_{Y_k})$ on $Z$ and the factorizations of the earlier radius functions through $\pi_{Y_k}$ let one lift first through the earlier joint radius map and then through the maximal pair, proving surjectivity of the joint radius map on $Z$. In constant-rank coordinates the inequalities $\rho_{Y_j}\ge d_j$ are independent half-space coordinates, so the core is a smooth compact manifold with corners and every designated face or face intersection is a genuine corner face, which checks the corner-face compatibility premise of [F3] and [F4]. [F1, F5, A1, step 6.1, step 7.1]

9.1 The normal level-core map to a fixed base core, $\pi_X:Z\cap S_X(a)\to X$, is a proper corner submersion with compatible faces. For $Y<X$ the boundary coordinate $\rho_Y-d_Y$ is the pullback of the same base boundary coordinate under $\pi_X$, and for $X<Y<Z$ it is an extra source face coordinate; the pair-map factorization proves surjectivity of the joint differential $(d\pi_X,d\rho_{Y_1},\ldots,d\rho_{Y_k})$ for the extra source faces, and the preceding kernel argument also applies to the fixed equation $\rho_X=a$. Thus local smooth constant-rank charts put the map and all active faces in the form $(b,u)\mapsto b$, with base inequalities in the coordinates $b$, the corresponding source inequalities equal to those base inequalities, and extra source inequalities in the coordinates $u$; properness follows from the proved compactness of the truncated cores. [F1, F5, A1, step 6.1, step 8.1]

10.1 To obtain bundle charts choose a sufficiently small corner box in the base. For each base coordinate $b_i$ choose local smooth horizontal fields satisfying $d\pi_XV_i=\partial/\partial b_i$ and $dh_jV_i=0$ for every active extra source face-defining coordinate $h_j$; the joint differential just proved has a smooth right inverse giving these fields. Choose patches avoiding every inactive closed face and retaining every active one; a smooth subordinate partition preserves all these linear equations, and no derivative of a partition coefficient enters. A source face pulled back from the base automatically has the prescribed derivative of that base coordinate, so it must not incorrectly be required tangent to an outward base field. [F1, F5, A1, step 6.1, step 9.1]

11.1 On a compact inverse image finitely many extended smooth corner charts give a common short flow time. Flow each coordinate in a fixed order from a selected base point, possibly on a boundary face; the coordinate segment remains in the base orthant, extra source faces are invariant, and corresponding source faces follow the nonnegative base coordinates, so the source path remains in the corner manifold. Extend the smooth field temporarily across the coordinate hyperplanes in its chart to define the one-sided boundary flow and retain only the part with nonnegative base and fibre face coordinates. Compactness and the face constraints exclude finite-time exit, and reversing the coordinate flows returns to the selected fibre and supplies the smooth inverse. These products preserve every named face and the projection exactly, and a finite base cover gives genuine finite smooth bundle product trivializations, which are the additional hypothesis required by the relative smooth bundle-fitting author [F4]. [F1, F5, A1, step 6.1, step 10.1]

12.1 For a finite controlled space $W$ let $W^{(p)}$ be its union of strata of real dimension at most $p$, closed by the frontier axiom. Put $T_p(d)=\bigcup_{\dim Y\le p}\{\rho_Y<d\}$, and for a stratum $X$ of dimension $i$ put $X_d^0=X\setminus T_{i-1}(d)$. Every such core is a compact manifold with corners by step 8.1. For a top stratum $Z$ of dimension $n$ put $S_d^p(Z)=Z_d^0\cap\bigcup_{\dim Y\le p}\{\rho_Y=d\}$; intersections of these sets are genuine corner faces because incomparable tube domains are disjoint and the joint rank of the radii in every active chain has been proved. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1]

13.1 An interior $d$-triangulation triangulates all cores $X_d^0$, retains every intersection with a lower normal level as a subpolyhedron, and makes the level-to-base projections PL. A partial $(d,p)$-triangulation does the same on all lower-dimensional cores and only on $S_d^p(Z)$ for each top stratum. At every stage the prescribed faces and their intersections are full subcomplexes after one common barycentric subdivision. Smooth-core pieces and positive-width collar pieces carry the nondegenerate local inverse and tangent-star contract of [F3] and [F4]; this is not asserted at a singular collapsed end, and singular ends arise only in the final topological gluing. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 12.1]

14.1 The induction retains buffers: if $d'<d$, choose $d'<d''<d$, retain the prescribed pieces on a closed collar, and fit within the larger open collar. All objects are compact and there are finitely many strata and flags, so each supplier's local fine-approximation bounds have positive minima on each of the finitely many compact pieces and a finite subdivision satisfies them. There is no infinite process, and no claim that an arbitrary preassigned incompatible smooth boundary triangulation can be extended. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 13.1]

15.1 Given an already triangulated level $J=f^{-1}(S_X(d))$, attach the product $J\times[d',d]$ along $J\times\{d\}$ and map $(q,t)\mapsto R_X(t)f(q)$; this is an embedding onto the annular $X$-collar whose inverse records the outer level point and $\rho_X$. The product has a finite triangulation, for instance by ordering simplex vertices and decomposing each simplex prism into finitely many monotone staircase simplices, with the same vertex order on shared faces; restrict this subdivision to every marked face. If several collars are extended, the radial commutation identity makes their two product parameterizations agree on overlap, including their corner parameters, so a common subdivision of the finitely many product faces glues them without changing their maps. Every radius preserved by a transport has the same marked level set before and after extension, and every lower projection transported equivariantly retains its induced PL coordinate expression; this is the precise sense in which extension is independent of the order of incidence of collar operations. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 14.1]

16.1 The mutually inductive assertions are $B_n$: extend an interior triangulation of the lower skeleton to an interior triangulation of an $n$-dimensional space after decreasing $d$; and $C_{(n,p)}$: extend a partial top-boundary triangulation through the faces whose lower controlling stratum has dimension $p$, after decreasing $d$. The order is $B_{n-1}$, then $C_{(n,0)},\ldots,C_{(n,n-1)}$, then $B_n$. The base consists of compact zero-dimensional cores, which are finite because each point is open in its zero-manifold and compactness gives a finite subcover by singleton neighbourhoods. The relative strengthening retains the prescribed finite collar faces and their inherited projections, and every application below is to boundary data produced by the preceding collar and core construction, with the star contract and compatible corners; it is not an unrestricted relative triangulation theorem for arbitrary subsets. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 15.1]

17.1 For $C_{(n,p)}$ process the $p$-dimensional lower strata $X$ separately; their tubes are disjoint. Work at the original outer level $S_X(d)$, reserving $d'<d''<d$. The already triangulated portion consists of its intersections with the lower skeleton and the top boundary faces previously handled by $C_{(n,q)}$ for $q<p$. Extend those prescribed portions along every other lower collar to the intermediate parameter $d''$; their intersections with $S_X(d)$ are still subpolyhedra by radius preservation. Pass to the compact closure of the level link, whose controlled structure and strict dimension drop were proved in steps 6.1 and 7.1, and apply the already completed dimension-$(n-1)$ interior and partial extension induction to that link, retaining the prescribed collar intersections. This triangulates all lower link pieces and every required boundary of the still untriangulated top link core. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 16.1]

18.1 The map to the fixed triangulated $X$-core is PL on this prescribed portion. On a portion controlled by a higher stratum $Y>X$ it factors as the inherited link projection to $Y\cap S_X(d)$ followed by the already triangulated map to $X$, and both factors are PL by the induction data. On portions near a lower $Y<X$ it is equivariant with the previously defined collar transports, so the product coordinate maps are the transported old PL maps. All these factorizations hold on actual tube overlaps, and the radius equations keep their source and target in the retained cores. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 17.1]

19.1 The relative bundle prerequisite is a diagram on an entire closed collar, not merely on its boundary; it is supplied before fitting. Extend every already triangulated boundary face by a positive-width radial product collar. For a controller $Y>X$ one has $\pi_XR_Y=\pi_X$, so the affine diagram map ignores that collar coordinate; for $Y<X$ one has $\pi_XR_Y=R_Y|_X\pi_X$, and the fixed target triangulation is extended by the identical $Y$-collar operation, so the diagram map carries that collar coordinate identically to the base. On multiple-face intersections the radial families commute and give the same product coordinate maps in either order. Thus $\pi_XF=hr$ holds throughout the closed collar and $r$ is PL after a common product subdivision; a smaller collar is protected and the positive-width buffer separates every later fitting support from it. This is the actual collar-neighbourhood hypothesis of [F4], not an assertion that a manifold boundary-extension theorem automatically preserves a bundle projection. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 18.1]

20.1 What remains in the top link stratum is a smooth compact manifold-with-corners core whose map to the fixed $X$-core has the actual finite face-compatible bundle charts proved in steps 9.1-11.1. The relative smooth bundle theorem [F4] triangulates it over that fixed base, making the projection PL; the projection-preserving fitting supplier fits it to the retained positive-width boundary collar, fixes the prescribed subcomplex and retains the projection exactly. The nondegenerate local star premise holds on both pieces, being supplied for the smooth core by [F3] and for the collar by the product construction. Full-subcomplex intersections follow from the fitting contract and a common subdivision. Transport the resulting entire link triangulation radially from $\rho_X=d$ to $\rho_X=d'$; its projection to $X$ does not change and its intersections with all previously treated collar faces agree with the previous partial extension, because the $X$-radial transport commutes with those transports and preserves their radii. Glue along those common full subcomplexes. This constructs $C_{(n,p)}$ using only smaller-dimensional induction and the proved smooth bundle-fitting interface. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 19.1]

21.1 For $B_n$ use the completed $C_{(n,p)}$ to triangulate every top-stratum boundary at an intermediate parameter $d''$, and extend this boundary triangulation to parameter $d'$ by the collar operator. The remaining portion of each top stratum is a smooth compact manifold with corners; apply the relative manifold triangulation theorem of [F3] and the ordinary finite-fitting clause of [F4] to that core, retaining its already triangulated closed boundary collar, so no bundle structure on the generic top core is required. The shared collar has the star contract and a buffer, and every face intersection is a genuine corner face; a finite simultaneous subdivision makes the overlaps full subcomplexes. Gluing the finite core and collar complexes gives the interior triangulation, the already lower-dimensional pieces and their boundary projections retain their maps, and only finitely many $(n,p)$ assertions occur, so finitely many decreases of $d$ leave a positive final parameter. [F1, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 11.1, step 20.1]

22.1 Fix the resulting interior triangulation $g_n:J_n\to W$; its image is the disjoint union of all stratum cores. Descend in $i$, with the invariant that the image of $g_i$ is this union plus $W\setminus T_{i-1}(d)$, that all stratum portions and future lower level sets are subpolyhedra, and that the projection from every future lower level to its current base portion is PL. Only these future projections need be retained; no claim is made that every old higher projection becomes a PL map on the completed space. [F1, F2, step 21.1]

23.1 For a stratum $X$ of dimension $i-1$ let $A_X=g_i^{-1}(S_X(d))$ and $B_X=g_i^{-1}(X)$; the base portion is precisely $X_d^0$ because the smaller-dimensional frontier tubes have not yet been filled, and the normal level portion is correspondingly truncated over this base, hence compact, with PL projection $f_X:A_X\to B_X$ by the invariant. Finite subdivision makes it simplicial by an explicit finite polytope construction: cut the target by the affine-hull and facet hyperplanes of the images of every face of every source simplex on which the map is affine, so every such image is a union of resulting target cells; cut each source simplex by the inverse images of these target cells. Every face of a source cell is a source face intersected with the inverse image of a target face, so its image is one target cell or empty, because the target refinement has already made every original source-face image a union of cells. For each nonempty source cell choose an interior point mapping to the chosen interior point of its image target cell, which exists because an affine surjection of a convex polytope onto its image sends relative interior onto relative interior. Cone the face subdivisions using these points and barycentrically cone the target cells; nested source faces have nested image target faces, with repetitions allowed, so the resulting map is simplicial. Mark all intersections with future lower levels and stratum closures, and apply one further barycentric subdivision to make all these marked subcomplexes full. [F1, F2, step 21.1, step 22.1]

24.1 Use the mapping-cylinder helper [F2] for $f_X$, allowing simplex vertex identifications; its finite domain and explicit homeomorphism with threshold inverse have already been constructed. Map its topological cylinder to $W$ by $(q,t)\mapsto R_X(td)g_i(q)$ for $t>0$, with the zero end mapped to $\pi_Xg_i(q)$. [F1] supplies continuity at that zero end and the homeomorphism onto the closed $X$-collar over $X_d^0$. The new collar meets the old image only in its outer level $A_X$ and base $B_X$: every old higher collar began at a core with $\rho_X\ge d$ and its radial transports preserve $\rho_X$, so no old point has $0<\rho_X<d$ over this base; two distinct same-dimensional $X$-collars are disjoint because their tubes are incomparable. Thus gluing along the two boundary copies is injective; the domain is finite compact, the target $W$ is Hausdorff, and the radial inverse proves surjectivity onto exactly the newly filled collar, so the map onto the new image is a homeomorphism. [F1, F2, step 21.1, step 23.1]

25.1 For a future lower stratum $Y<X$ the functions $\rho_Y$ and $\pi_Y$ factor through $\pi_X$ on the $X$-collar, so the part of $S_Y(d)$ inside this new cylinder is exactly the cylinder over the corresponding marked source and base subcomplex pair; the mapping-cylinder helper makes it a subpolyhedron, and its projection to the future $Y$-base is the cylinder retraction followed by the existing base projection $\pi_Y|_X$, both PL. This proves the descending invariant. Stratum-closure intersections are retained by the same subcylinder compatibility, because the radial maps preserve strata, so an upper stratum or its closure contributes its marked top subset together with the appropriate zero-end base subset. No dimension used here is a complex perversity dimension. [F1, F2, step 21.1, step 24.1]

26.1 After all $i$ have been processed the image is $W$, and all strata and prescribed unions of strata are unions of open simplices. The complex dimension is at most the maximal real stratum dimension: smooth core complexes have their manifold dimension, link dimensions drop by one, and the mapping-cylinder dimension bound of [F2] adds at most one to the source-link dimension while retaining the smaller base dimension. The finite simplicial cylinder maps are smooth inside positive-height cells, and radial transport is smooth on each smooth stratum; at a zero end the lower stratum already has its smooth core triangulation, and no ambient smooth immersion through a singular end is asserted. The finite list of glued complexes therefore supplies the claimed finite compatible stratified triangulation by the preceding interior construction and the exact relative-supplier premises. [F1, F2, step 21.1, step 25.1] ∎

items.title: Finite simplicial open stars have explicit conical product charts
items.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex and let $\sigma$ be a nonempty simplex.
Let $\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma$ be the subcomplex of simplices $\tau$ disjoint
from $\sigma$ with $\sigma\cup\tau\in K$, and let $\operatorname{st}_K(\sigma)$
be the open star of $\sigma$
([[def-simplicial-subcomplex-star-closure-and-link]]). Then
$$\operatorname{st}_K(\sigma)\cong\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|),$$
where $c_{<1}(L)=(L\times[0,1))/(L\times\{0\})$ with the quotient topology, and
the cone on the empty space means a single apex. The homeomorphism takes each
simplex interior containing $\sigma$ to the product with the corresponding
link-simplex interior and positive radial coordinate; the simplex $\sigma$
itself maps to the apex. The link is compact and has finitely many simplices.
If $D\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex and $\sigma\notin D$, this star lies in
$|K|\setminus|D|$.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Put $L=|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|$ and let $E=\{rq:0\le r<1,\ q\in L\}$ inside the Euclidean coordinate space on the vertices of the link, with the subspace topology. For an empty link both the cone by convention and $E=\{0\}$ are a single apex, so assume $L\ne\varnothing$. The continuous map $L\times[0,1)\to E$, $(q,r)\mapsto rq$, identifies exactly $L\times\{0\}$ with the apex: if $rq=r'q'$ with $r,r'>0$, coordinate sums give $r=r'$ and then $q=q'$. It therefore descends to a continuous bijection $\varphi:c_{<1}(L)\to E$. For each $0<t<1$, the closed radial cone $(L\times[0,t])/(L\times\{0\})$ is compact by [F2], and its continuous bijection onto $E_t=\{rq:0\le r\le t,\ q\in L\}$ is a homeomorphism because $E_t$ is Hausdorff. Away from the apex the inverse on the full open cone is continuous by $r=\sum_vz_v$, $q=z/r$, followed by the quotient projection. At the apex, the preimage of any quotient-open neighbourhood is an open set containing $L\times\{0\}$. Product neighbourhoods of its points, a finite cover of the compact link $L$, and the minimum of their positive radii give an $\epsilon>0$ with $L\times[0,\epsilon)$ in that preimage. The relatively open set $\{z\in E:\sum_vz_v<\epsilon\}$ is consequently mapped by $\varphi^{-1}$ into the given neighbourhood. Thus the inverse is continuous at the apex too, and $\varphi$ is a homeomorphism of the full open cone. [F1, F2, construct]

2.1 For a point $x$ of the open star put $a=\sum_{v\in\sigma}x_v>0$, set $p_v=x_v/a$ for $v\in\sigma$ and $z_v=x_v$ for $v\notin\sigma$. Then $p\in\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|$, $r:=\sum_vz_v=1-a<1$, and the support of $x$ is $\sigma\cup\operatorname{supp}(z)$, so $\operatorname{supp}(z)$, if nonempty, is a simplex of the link. Conversely, given $p\in\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|$ and $z\in E$ with $r=\sum_vz_v$, define a coordinate family by $x_v=(1-r)p_v$ on $\sigma$ and $x_v=z_v$ off $\sigma$; it is nonnegative with sum one, and its support is $\sigma\cup\operatorname{supp}(z)$, a simplex of $K$ because $\operatorname{supp}(z)$ is a simplex of the link. The two constructions are mutually inverse: from $x$ one recovers $a=1-r$ and $z$, hence $x$; from $(p,z)$ one recovers $p$ from the normalized $\sigma$-coordinates and $z$ from the outside coordinates. Both are continuous, the only division being by $a>0$ on the open star for the forward map, while the inverse is a polynomial expression in $(p,z)$ and the continuous function $r=\sum_vz_v$. By step 1.1 the second factor is the cone $c_{<1}(L)$, and since $\operatorname{supp}(z)$ records exactly which link simplex the radial coordinate lies over, each simplex interior containing $\sigma$ is carried to the product of the corresponding link-simplex interior with $(0,1)$, while points with $z=0$ map to $\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times\{\mathrm{apex}\}$ and the simplex $\sigma$ itself to the apex. Thus the star is homeomorphic to the stated product. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The open star is open in $|K|$ because it is the finite intersection, over the vertices of $\sigma$, of the sets on which one barycentric coordinate is positive, each open in the weak topology by definition. The link is a subcomplex of the finite complex $K$, hence it has finitely many simplices and compact realization by [F2]. Finally, if a point $x$ of the star lay in $|D|$, its support would be a simplex $\rho$ of $D$ with $\sigma\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(x)=\rho$; the subcomplex $D$ is closed under taking faces, so $\sigma\in D$, contradicting $\sigma\notin D$. Hence the star is disjoint from $|D|$. [F1, F2, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: Finite cell local system cohomology is finite and commutes with field extension
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(X,A)$ be a finite CW pair of dimension $d$, let $k$ be a field
and let $L$ be a $k$-vector-space local system with finite-dimensional fibres
([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). Then $H^q(X,A;L)$ is
finite-dimensional, vanishes for $q<0$ and $q>d$, and for every field extension
$k\subseteq k'$ the natural map is an isomorphism:
$$H^q(X,A;L)\otimes_k k'\cong H^q(X,A;L\otimes_k k').$$
The assertion holds separately on every component, including the empty pair.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Work first on one component, with basepoint $x$, group $\pi=\pi_1(X,x)$ and fibre $M=L_x$. By [F1] the degree-$q$ term of the cellular local cochain complex is $\operatorname{Hom}_{k[\pi]}(P_q,M)$ with $P_q$ free over $k[\pi]$ on the finitely many relative $q$-cells of the component, so choosing that finite basis identifies it with the finite product $M^{n_q}$; since $M$ is finite-dimensional, the term is finite-dimensional, and it is zero for $q<0$ and for $q>d$. By [F2] the cohomology $H^q(X,A;L)$ is the cohomology of this complex, so it is finite-dimensional as a kernel, image or quotient of finite-dimensional spaces and vanishes outside $[0,d]$. For a disconnected pair the cochain complex is the degreewise product of the complexes of the finitely many components, and the same conclusions hold componentwise; the empty pair has the zero complex. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

2.1 Let $k'$ be a field extension and give $M\otimes_kk'$ the induced $k'[\pi]$-module structure; these fibres with the extended transport maps form the local system $L\otimes_kk'$. The termwise map $\operatorname{Hom}_{k[\pi]}(P_q,M)\otimes_kk'\to\operatorname{Hom}_{k'[\pi]}(P_q\otimes_kk',M\otimes_kk')$, defined on a basis of the free module $P_q$, is an isomorphism, because both sides identify with $(M\otimes_kk')^{n_q}$; it is natural in the second variable and therefore intertwines the differentials, which are obtained by dualizing the same $k[\pi]$-linear cellular boundary of [F2]. Hence $C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;L)\otimes_kk'$ is isomorphic, as a complex, to $C^*_{\mathrm{cell}}(X,A;L\otimes_kk')$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F3] the field $k'$, viewed as a $k$-vector space, is free and hence flat, so tensoring over $k$ with $k'$ preserves exact sequences. Applying this to the kernel-image sequences of the complex of step 1.1 gives a canonical isomorphism $H^q\bigl(C^*\otimes_kk'\bigr)\cong H^q(C^*)\otimes_kk'$, which by step 2.1 and [F2] is the stated map $H^q(X,A;L)\otimes_kk'\to H^q(X,A;L\otimes_kk')$, natural in the coefficients. The finiteness, the vanishing outside $[0,d]$, and the isomorphism all hold separately on each component and for the empty pair, where both complexes vanish. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
