items.title: Algebraically constructible sheaves have finite compatible stratified and local cochain models
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X$ be a quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, $k$ a
field, and $F$ a bounded complex of analytic $k$-sheaves whose cohomology is
locally constant of finite rank on a finite complex algebraic stratification.
Fix finitely many algebraic supports and locally closed inclusions to be
respected. There is a finite compatible smooth complex algebraic Whitney
refinement, a projective compactification with its algebraic boundary
respected, and a finite pair of simplicial complexes $(K,D)$ such that
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong|K|\setminus|D|$, every open simplex lies in one complex
stratum, and the marked supports are unions of simplices. One can take
$\dim K\le2\dim_{\mathbb C}X$; in particular constant-sheaf cohomology vanishes
above that real dimension. The same construction applies individually to the
compact controlled links supplied by the conical-neighborhood theorem.

On these models, actual ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary
derived Hom, internal derived Hom and local cohomology with a prescribed
algebraic support have bounded finite-dimensional cochain models. Internal Hom
is constructible on a finite complex Whitney refinement. The local link and
support models vary locally constantly along the corresponding complex strata;
thus their cohomology has finite rank there. Every such model commutes with
extension of the coefficient field. Inclusions and supports are chosen in
finite collections for a given construction; no compatible triangulation of
arbitrary algebraic maps or cyclic diagrams is asserted. Perverse dimensions
remain the dimensions of the complex strata, independent of the auxiliary real
simplices.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By quasi-projectivity choose an algebraic locally closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N$. Its reduced projective closure $\overline X$ has $X$ as an open subset, and $B=\overline X\setminus X$ is closed algebraic. Take closures of the finitely many marked supports and the pieces of the given constructibility stratification. Apply [F1]'s connected finite Whitney stratification construction to the identity morphism of $\overline X$, respecting these closed algebraic subsets and their finite locally closed differences. This gives a complex Whitney refinement on which every cohomology sheaf of $F$ stays finite-rank locally constant; passing to smaller smooth strata preserves local constancy. The compact analytic space $\overline X^{\mathrm{an}}$ embeds smoothly in a finite Euclidean space: send a projective line represented by $z\ne0$ to its Hermitian rank-one projector $zz^*/(z^*z)$. This is well-defined, injective, and smooth in the projective coordinate charts; its chart inverse recovers the ratios of the projector's nonzero column, so it is a smooth embedding. It is compact because it is the continuous image of the unit sphere. Its restricted algebraic Whitney strata satisfy the real smooth Whitney conditions used by [F2]. Apply [F2], including all chosen stratum unions. Let $K$ be the resulting finite complex and $D$ the subcomplex mapping onto $B$; one barycentric subdivision makes every marked subcomplex full if needed. Restricting the homeomorphism yields $X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong |K|\setminus|D|$ as claimed. [given, F1, F2, A1, construct]

2.1 Every retained open simplex is contained in one original complex stratum. The cohomology of $F$ on it is finite-rank locally constant, so $F$ belongs to the actual essential image of [F4]. It therefore has a bounded finite-dimensional diagram representative on the face poset of the retained simplices, with no assertion that the analytic sheaf category itself is finite. The finite bar construction of [F5] computes actual ordinary derived global sections and actual derived Hom because [F4] proves full faithfulness against the analytic sheaf category by independently established star acyclicity. Its compact-support clause identifies the actual support functor with finite relative cochains on the compactification pair; this uses the c-soft acyclicity and open extension by zero declared in [F4]. Finite simplicial stars and their closed subcomplex complements admit the explicit finite product/cone models of [F3]. Thus local support cohomology is computed by the finite cone of restriction from such a neighborhood to its complement of the marked support, with the conventional shift determined by the support triangle. These restrictions and their maps are the actual sheaf restrictions under [F4], not merely vector spaces with matching dimensions. For the constant sheaf on a compact model the ordinary cellular model has no cochain terms above the simplicial dimension, which is at most twice the complex dimension by [F2]. All face-chain lengths and cohomology amplitudes are finite, so the models are uniformly bounded for the finitely many chosen strata and supports. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 The ordinary incidence calculation alone gives constructibility on real simplices. To obtain local constancy along a complex stratum $S$, use [F1]'s actual local chart $U\cong V\times cL$, where $V$ is a small contractible ball in $S$ and the chart preserves the complex strata. The compact link $L$ has a finite inherited controlled stratification and a finite triangulation by [F2], and $cL$ truncated to a finite radius has a finite deleted-boundary model. Each product stratum is a product of the contractible $V$ with a link stratum. The restriction of the cohomology sheaves of $F$ is locally constant there. On a link simplex, therefore, its restriction to $V$ times that simplex is represented by a finite coefficient complex independent of the $V$ direction. This last derived assertion follows from [F4], rather than assuming a sheaf is invariant under every stratum-preserving homeomorphism: pullback along the projection to the link is fully faithful on the relevant finite incidence categories because [F4]'s product comparison has fibre $V$ and $C^*(V;k)\simeq k$ by [F3]. Filter the finitely many link simplices by closed skeleta. On a simplex piece the object is a pullback: finite-rank constant sheaves on the contractible product have no positive Ext between them by [F4] and its constant-sheaf comparison. The finite ordinary truncation triangles therefore split there, expressing its locally constant bounded complex by a finite coefficient complex. The ordinary exact open/closed extension-by-zero triangles in [F4] build the object through this finite filtration. Full faithfulness lifts the connecting morphisms between pullbacks, so their finite cones are again pullbacks. Induction proves that the restriction of $F$ to this chart is pulled back from a finite link-cone object. The same argument applies simultaneously to the chosen finite collection of input objects and marked support strata. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 2.1]

4.1 In step 3.1's chart, ordinary local sections, punctured-neighborhood sections and sections with a marked support are therefore the corresponding finite link/cone cochains, constant in the $V$ direction. Their restriction morphisms are the product/incidence morphisms, so their support cones are locally constant too. Applying this also to two input complexes shows that their internal derived Hom is locally constant in the $V$ direction, with bounded finite-dimensional stalks computed by [F4] and [F5]. Finitely many complex Whitney strata give a uniform amplitude bound. Hence the result is constructible for the complex stratification (or its finite simultaneous support refinement), not merely for the real simplex partition. This is the local constructibility and finite local cohomology assertion required for the later open/closed and perverse gluing constructions. It does not substitute the real simplex dimension for the complex dimension of $S$. [F1, F4, F5, step 3.1]

5.1 Finally every displayed incidence, bar, relative support and link-cone model is a finite matrix complex of finite-dimensional $k$-spaces. Tensor with a field extension $k\subset k'$ is exact, carries its kernels and images to the corresponding kernels and images, and commutes with every finite sum, differential, restriction map and cone. The comparisons of [F4] and the finite local-system comparison of [F3] therefore identify these scalar-extended complexes with the actual corresponding sheaf constructions over $k'$. The constructions and comparisons are locally coherent through their actual incidence morphisms. This proves all claimed finite cohomology and coefficient-extension assertions. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For quasi-projective complex varieties and
finitely many algebraic operations/support collections, the geometric suppliers
give individually chosen compatible smooth Whitney strata, conical local
products and finite deleted-boundary triangulation models for each operation.
No simultaneous stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram respecting all
marked supports is asserted. On any separated finite-type complex variety,
bounded algebraically constructible objects have bounded finite ordinary and
compact-support cohomology, ordinary derived Hom and bounded constructible
internal Hom, with coefficient-extension compatibility, by these models locally
and finite affine-open descent globally. A noncompact variety is not asserted
to be a finite compact realization.

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 **The needed ordinary operations and field injectives.** Inverse image is exact because its stalks are the corresponding source stalks, and the inverse/direct-image adjunction of [F7] is $k$-linear. Consequently direct image carries injectives to injectives: its representable functor is the composite of exact inverse image and the exact injective representable functor. Compute ordinary $Rf_*$ and derived Hom by the supplied bounded-below $k$-linear injective replacements. Their comparison maps and ordinary direct-image composition are the injective-model comparisons of [F7]. The bounded internal Hom used in the geometric argument is the actual sheaf object computed by the derived-incidence supplier [F4], not Hom of the stalks. To check that a $k$-injective sheaf $I$ is flasque, for open $U\subseteq V$ use the stalkwise monomorphism $j_{U!}k_U\to j_{V!}k_V$. The adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(j_{U!}k_U,I)=I(U)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(j_{V!}k_V,I)=I(V)$; a map from the constant sheaf is determined by the image of $1$, and every section determines such a map by locally constant scalar multiplication. Injectivity therefore makes $I(V)\to I(U)$ surjective. By [F8], $I$ is c-soft and its open/closed restrictions and their extensions by zero are c-soft. The underlying abelian sheaves of a $k$-injective resolution are flasque, hence acyclic for ordinary sections by [F7]; the acyclic-resolution theorem therefore identifies its section cohomology with the underlying abelian sheaf cohomology. For compact supports on a locally compact Hausdorff space, the same comparison uses the c-soft acyclicity of those underlying resolution terms from [F8]. Thus the compact c-soft acyclicity of [F8] applies also to the $k$-linear derived sections used here, without assuming a $k$-injective sheaf is injective after forgetting scalars. All these constructions are natural in sheaf morphisms. [given, F4, F7, F8, A1, construct, algebra]

2.1 **Proper maps: the actual fibre comparison.** Let $p:Z\to Y$ be a proper continuous map between locally compact Hausdorff spaces, where proper means inverse images of compact subsets are compact. It is closed: for a closed $C\subseteq Z$ and a relatively compact base neighbourhood $W$, the set $C\cap p^{-1}(\overline W)$ is compact and its image is closed, and on $W$ that image equals $p(C)\cap W$. If $Z_y=p^{-1}(y)$ is contained in an open $O\subseteq Z$, then $Y\setminus p(Z\setminus O)$ is an open neighbourhood of $y$ whose inverse image lies in $O$. Thus inverse images of base neighbourhoods are cofinal among neighbourhoods of the compact fibre. Apply the compact-section theorem [F8] degreewise to an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ supplied by [F7]: the stalk complex $(p_*I^\bullet)_y$ is naturally $\Gamma(Z_y,I^\bullet|_{Z_y})$. Restriction to $Z_y$ is exact, and its terms are c-soft by step 1.1, hence ordinary-section acyclic because the fibre is compact. Therefore $\Gamma(Z_y,I^\bullet|_{Z_y})$ computes $R\Gamma(Z_y,F|_{Z_y})$ by the acyclic-resolution theorem. This proves the canonical proper fibre formula $(Rp_*F)_y\simeq R\Gamma(Z_y,F|_{Z_y})$ and its natural restriction maps, with no later six-operation theorem. The same proof works for bounded complexes by bounded-below injective replacement. Exact filtered colimits in [F8] justify passing from the stalk complex to its cohomology. [given, F7, F8, A1, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 **Proper-support sections on an open-proper factorization.** For $f:X\to Y$ factoring as an open inclusion $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ followed by proper $p:Z\to Y$, define $f_!F$ on $V\subseteq Y$ as sections of $F$ on $f^{-1}(V)$ whose closed support maps properly to $V$. This is exactly $p_*j_!F$. Indeed a section of $j_!F$ has support closed in $p^{-1}(V)$, so restriction of the proper map $p$ to that support is proper. Conversely a support proper over $V$ has no boundary accumulation in $p^{-1}(V)\setminus X$: near a proposed boundary point choose a relatively compact base neighbourhood $W$ with closure in $V$; the support over $\overline W$ is compact in $X$, hence compact and closed in $Z$, and cannot accumulate at that boundary point. Thus zero extension is an actual section of $j_!F$. These inverse section maps commute with restriction and give the sheaf identity $f_!=p_*j_!$; it is a left exact $k$-linear sheaf functor and does not depend on the chosen factorization. A section's support is closed because zero germs form an open set. This construction uses only support, properness and exact extension by zero; no exceptional inverse image or trace is needed. [given, F7, F8, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 **Derivation and finite open-cover support descent.** For an injective $I$ on $X$, the sheaf $j_!I$ restricts to a c-soft sheaf on each compact fibre of $p$: first restrict the c-soft $I$ of step 1.1 to the open fibre part and then extend by zero; both operations preserve c-softness by [F8]. Step 2.1 applied to $j_!I$ therefore gives $R^qp_*j_!I=0$ for $q>0$, since its fibre cohomology vanishes in positive degree. The exact functor $j_!$ carries an injective replacement $A\to I^\bullet$ to a $p_*$-acyclic replacement, so the acyclic-resolution theorem gives the actual factorization $Rf_!A=Rp_*j_!A$. Its fibre is $R\Gamma(Z_y,j_!A|_{Z_y})=R\Gamma_c(X_y,A|_{X_y})$, the last equality being the open/closed compact-support identity of [F8]. These are the canonical section restriction comparisons. They are independent of the open-proper factorization because step 3.1 identifies the same underived functor and the same derived injective model. For a finite open cover $(U_a)$ of a source, the augmented alternating complex of the sheaves $j_{U_{a_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{a_r}!}(A|_{U_{a_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{a_r}})$ resolves $A$: at each stalk its augmented complex is the exact simplex complex on the nonempty set of cover members containing that point. After replacing $A$ by injectives, each term is c-soft on the relevant source opens and their fibre restrictions. On every quasi-projective piece the preceding graph-factorization calculation makes these terms acyclic for its proper-support functor. Applying the proper-support functor to this finite resolution and its bounded-below injective models therefore gives the finite open-cover support descent used below, with exact augmented columns and finite diagonals. Coefficient extension commutes with the finite local cochains by [F4]; the finite descent complexes preserve that comparison. Ordinary $Rf_*$ composition is supplied by step 1.1. [given, F4, F5, F7, F8, A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 For each individual quasi-projective map and support collection, apply the actual compatible-stratification and control suppliers, followed by their fixed-space triangulation supplier. This is the precise geometric scope actually authored upstream. On each supplied finite deleted-boundary model the incidence theorem proves the finite local/global cochains, internal-Hom constructibility and field-extension comparison. Choices for different operations need not form one jointly stratified cyclic diagram. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 4.1]

6.1 A separated finite-type variety has a finite affine-open cover, whose finite intersections are affine: its closed diagonal identifies each two-chart intersection with a closed subscheme of the affine chart product, and iterate. Each intersection is quasi-projective. Apply the local geometric/incidence construction there. The actual finite open-cover Cech derived augmentation assembles their cochains. Only finitely many intersection degrees occur, and the finitely many local cohomology bounds give a uniform finite total bound. Hence ordinary/global derived Hom and cohomology are bounded and finite, and their finite complexes commute with field extension. Compact-support models are assembled by the ordinary open/closed support resolution and the same finite local models. Internal Hom is locally computed on the finite affine cover and its bounds are uniform. For an explicit global witness to algebraic constructibility, take the finite collections of locally closed strata from all affine charts and their finite overlap refinements; these are locally closed algebraic subsets of the whole variety. Prescribe their closures and closed boundaries in [F1]'s identity-map smooth frontier construction. Every resulting connected smooth algebraic stratum lies in one chart stratum, so the internal-Hom cohomology remains locally constant of finite rank on it. This supplies a finite global constructibility witness without asserting a quasi-projective compactification or a global Whitney theorem for the general separated variety. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, A1, step 4.1, step 5.1]

7.1 For one morphism between quasi-projective varieties, choose a locally closed embedding of its source into $\mathbb P^N$ and take the reduced closure of its graph in $\mathbb P^N\times Y$. The graph is locally closed, hence open in that closure; thus the map factors as an open inclusion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ followed by the projective projection $p:\overline X\to Y$. The closure is quasi-projective and $p$ is analytically proper by [F1]. Each algebraic fibre has a deleted-boundary model of dimension at most twice the source dimension by [F3]; [F6] therefore bounds compact-support cohomology of every sheaf on every fibre open by that same integer. Thus the support operations satisfy their required all-fibre-open hypothesis, rather than merely a bound for constructible coefficients. Choose [F1]'s one-map Whitney strata for $p$, respecting the boundary $\overline X\setminus X$ and the finite input supports. Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact; $Rj_*$ is locally computed by the ordinary sections on the open part of [F2]'s controlled link-cone chart, and [F3] and [F4] give the bounded finite, locally constant complex-stratum model and its actual restriction maps. The proper whole-fibre local trivializations of [F2] give, over a small ball in each target stratum, a product with a compact stratified fibre. The same derived product reconstruction used in [F3] identifies the constructible input there with a fibre object constant in the ball direction, so its pushforward is its finite fibre cochain complex constant along that ball. Finitely many target strata give a uniform amplitude bound; ordinary direct-image composition (inverse image is exact, so direct image preserves injectives) and the proper-support factorization of step 4.1 show $Rp_*Rj_*$ and $Rp_*j_!$ compute $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ respectively. All models and comparisons commute with field extension by [F3] and [F4]. For a general separated finite-type map, work over an affine target chart, take a finite affine cover of its source preimage and finite intersections, and apply this construction to their finite disjoint union mapping to the target. Prescribe the needed supports in that one-map construction, obtaining one target stratification for the finitely many terms. The actual finite open-cover derived augmentation of [F5] then assembles ordinary pushforward; its extension-by-zero support resolution of step 4.1 assembles proper-support pushforward. Thus the outputs are bounded algebraically constructible locally on the target and hence globally by a finite affine cover. This proof uses a constructed projective factorization on each quasi-projective piece and proper whole-fibre triviality, rather than inferring whole-fibre control from local source charts. No joint stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram is required. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1] ∎

items.title: A noncompact algebraic line needs a deleted boundary triangulation
items.statement: The analytic complex affine line $\mathbb A^1(\mathbb C)=\mathbb C$ cannot be homeomorphic to the realization of a finite simplicial complex. It is homeomorphic to a finite triangulated compactification with one boundary vertex deleted. Thus "finite triangulation" for noncompact varieties must allow a deleted subcomplex or another equivalent noncompact finite-cell convention.
items.strategy: (1) The increasing open disks $\{|z|<n\}$ cover $\mathbb C$ but no finite subfamily does, so $\mathbb C$ is not compact; since finite simplicial realizations are compact ([[prop-a-finite-simplicial-complex-has-compact-hausdorff-realization]]), no finite realization is homeomorphic to $\mathbb C$. (2) The boundary complex $K$ of the octahedron realizes the $\ell^1$-sphere in $\mathbb R^3$; radial normalization and its inverse identify $|K|$ with $S^2$, and deleting the vertex $e_3$ gives $S^2\setminus\{e_3\}$. (3) The stereographic formula $(a,b)\mapsto(2a,2b,a^2+b^2-1)/(a^2+b^2+1)$ is a homeomorphism $\mathbb C\to S^2\setminus\{e_3\}$ with inverse $u\mapsto(u_1,u_2)/(1-u_3)$. Hence $\mathbb C$ is a finite complex with one vertex deleted, which is the compactification convention used by the finite triangulation statements on the companion page.
